The timing of this crash is notable. It comes just one day before the US Federal Reserve announces its interest rate decision, and the uncertainty around a potential rate hike has weighed heavily on risk-on assets like cryptocurrencies.

Bitcoin fell nearly $3,000 from its Monday high of $65,600 to around $63,000, marking a ten-day low and erasing all gains from the previous day's rally.

# $700 Million in Liquidations as BTC Plunges to Ten-Day Low

$700 Million in liquidations were recorded in the past 24 hours as Bitcoin crashed to a ten-day low around $63,000. The leading cryptocurrency had surged to $65,600 on Monday, but that rally has come to an abrupt end. This sharp reversal dragged most major altcoins down with it, triggering approximately $700 million in liquidations across the crypto market in just 24 hours. [CryptoPotato](https://cryptopotato.com/700-million-in-liquidations-as-btc-eth-xrp-plunge-ahead-of-fomc/) and [CoinGape](https://coingape.com/crypto-market-crash-700m-in-bitcoin-ethereum-xrp-solana-ai-coins-liquidated-heres-why/) reported on the cascading liquidations that wiped out over 165,000 traders.

Popular analyst CRYPTOWZRD noted that Bitcoin closed in bearish territory and emphasized the importance of holding the $63,000 support level. Should BTC break below this threshold, the analyst warned it could slump to new local lows.

### Resistance Failure Triggers Technical Selloff

The double rejection at $65,600 triggered automated selling as traders exited positions. Technical analysts point to the violation of the $64,000 support zone as a key bearish signal. Market depth data showed decreasing buy orders at lower price levels, indicating weak dip-buying interest.

## Ethereum and Altcoins Follow BTC Lower

Ethereum was the top gainer just a day ago, surging to a two-month peak of $1,980. However, the tables turned quickly. ETH has lost $100 since then and now trades well below $1,900, with liquidations exceeding those of Bitcoin in percentage terms. The decline was even more pronounced for XRP, which dumped 4.5% to $1.06, slipping below the coveted $1.10 support level that traders had been watching closely.

### Major Altcoins Post Double-Digit Losses

Solana followed a similar trajectory, down roughly 4.5% on the day. Hyperliquid's native token HYPE took the hardest hit among major altcoins, plummeting 6%. Beyond the top-tier coins, the damage was even more severe. Top altcoins including BNB, Cardano, and Bitcoin Cash fell 2-7%, while meme coins Dogecoin, Shiba Inu, and Pepe Coin dropped more than 4%.

TheCrypto Market Fear & Greed Index dropped sharply from 48 (neutral) to 28 (fear), reflecting the sudden and dramatic shift in market sentiment within just a few days.

## Over 165,000 Traders Wiped Out

This market move devastated over-leveraged traders. More than 165,000 participants were liquidated in the past 24 hours as the total value of liquidated positions climbed to nearly $700 million. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/crypto-market-crash-700m-bitcoin-065001264.html) covered the widespread liquidations across the ecosystem. Bitcoin and Ethereum naturally led the liquidation tally, but Solana, XRP, Cardano, and others also contributed significantly.

### Long Positions Bear the Brunt

The largest single liquidation order was an ETH-USDT position worth $28.49 million on crypto exchange Bitget. Long positions accounted for the bulk of the pain, with approximately $620 million in long positions liquidated compared to $80 million in short positions. Over $520 million in long positions were wiped out in just four hours, according to Coinglass data.

This marks one of the most severe liquidation events in recent months, with no signs of buy-the-dip sentiment emerging to steady the market.

## FOMC Uncertainty Fuels Crypto Selloff

The timing of this crash is notable. It comes just one day before the US Federal Reserve announces its interest rate decision, and the uncertainty around a potential rate hike has weighed heavily on risk-on assets like cryptocurrencies. The pending FOMC announcement has traders on edge, as any hawkish signals could extend the market correction.

### Macro Headwinds Intensify

Traders are closely watching the FOMC meeting for clues about the Fed's monetary policy path. CME FedWatch Tool data currently shows markets fully pricing out any rate cuts for the remainder of the year, with increasing bets on a possible rate hike before year-end. The macro uncertainty, combined with technical weakness in Bitcoin's price action, has created a perfect storm for the crypto market. Global cryptocurrency market capitalization has tumbled to $2.56 trillion, erasing more than $180 billion in value since last week.

## Conclusion

The $700 million liquidation event underscores the risks of leveraged trading in a market highly sensitive to macroeconomic headlines. Bitcoin's drop to a ten-day low and the broader altcoin selloff reflect trader anxiety ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate decision. Until clarity emerges on the Fed's policy direction, expect continued volatility across crypto markets.

**1. Why did the crypto market crash so sharply?**

The crash was driven by a combination of factors: Bitcoin's failure to break $65,600 resistance triggered technical selling, while uncertainty ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision made traders reduce risk exposure. The result was a cascade of liquidations totaling nearly $700 million.

Bitcoin fell nearly $3,000 from its Monday high of $65,600 to around $63,000, marking a ten-day low and erasing all gains from the previous day's rally.

The market crash highlights how sensitive crypto is to macroconomic policy expectations. Traders are bracing for a potentially hawkish Fed stance, which could keep pressure on risk assets including cryptocurrencies.

Ethereum saw the biggest drops among majors, falling from a two-month peak of $1,980 to below $1,900. XRP declined 4.5% to $1.06, while HYPE plummeted 6%. Meme coins Dogecoin, Shiba Inu, and Pepe Coin also fell over 4%.

**5. Are more liquidations likely?**

Given the heightened volatility and macro uncertainty surrounding the FOMC announcement, further liquidations remain possible if Bitcoin breaks below the critical $63,000 support level.
